B: Hiya! I'm Gemma. How's your day going?
A: Hello, I'm Ioana. It's okay, thank you. Quiet day. I start work later.
B: Oh, are you on lates? What do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
A: I am a cleaner at a primary school. In Colindale. After school, half past three to eight.
B: Oh, so you're the one who makes it all look nice for the morning. My mum did school dinners for years, so I've got a soft spot for school staff, you know? They do loads nobody sees.
A: Yes, nobody sees. It is fine. I like it when it is empty.
B: I bet it's nice and peaceful. Sorry, I'm in Warrington, by the way. I work in an office for a scaffolding firm, so it's never peaceful. It's lads shouting about where the tower is.
A: Scaffolding. Like on the buildings?
B: That's it. I do the accounts and the hire paperwork. Not glamorous, but I like it. Do you get your tea before you go in, or after?
A: Dinner after. Maybe nine, half past nine. My husband waits for me usually.
B: Oh, that's late! We have tea on the table by six, I'd be climbing the walls. What do you cook? Do you cook much?
A: Romanian food, mostly. Ciorbă, a sour soup, with lovage. Sarmale at Christmas, cabbage rolls. The shops on the Broadway have everything now. Even proper cheese, finally.
B: Oh, that sounds lovely. I do a big pan of scouse when it's cold, which is like a stew. I batch cook it on a Sunday after church.
A: You go to church?
B: Erm, I do, yeah. Not every week, sorry, I'm not that good. Christmas, Easter, harvest, and a few in between. It's a little parish church near me.
A: I saw maybe you would. In my photo there is an icon, Mary. I am Orthodox. I go at Easter, also Christmas. For the singing, mostly.
B: Oh, I didn't notice it, sorry. That's lovely though. I think it's the feeling, isn't it, more than anything. When my dad died, I didn't expect church to help, but it did. I light a candle for him.
A: Yes. At Easter we have candles too, at midnight. Everyone carries the light home. It is hard to say why it matters, but it does.
B: No, that makes sense. That's really nice, carrying it home. What do you do on your days off, then? Mornings, I suppose, if you're working evenings?
A: Museums. Galleries. National Gallery, Tate. I go alone and stay a long time.
B: Oh, I'll be honest, I don't really know much about art. I'm more of a musicals girl. I've seen Wicked and Mamma Mia! at the Palace in Manchester, and I cried at both, which Craig, that's my husband, finds hilarious.
A: Crying is good. That means it worked. Sometimes I go to Barbican, cheap tickets, very strange music. Mihai, my husband, comes once and he says never again.
B: Ha! Craig's the same with Strictly. He pretends he's not watching it and then he's got opinions on the foxtrot. Sorry, am I waffling?
A: No. It's nice. What is your favourite in Wicked?
